title: WHO CAN SURVIVE WHAT GOD DOES

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then he spoke his message: "Alas! Who can live when God does this? Ships will come from the shores of Cyprus; they will subdue Ashur and Eber, but they too will come to ruin." Then Balaam got up and returned home, and Balak went his own way. - Num 24:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam's final words carry a note of awe and dread: "Alas! Who can live when God does this?" He glimpses distant upheavals, empires rising and subduing one another, yet even the conquerors coming to ruin in the end. The whole vision underscores one truth: God stands sovereign over the tumult of history, and none can stand against His purposes.

Then, abruptly, the scene ends. Balaam gets up and returns home, and Balak goes his own way. After all the altars, oracles, and schemes, the two part with nothing changed except the clear demonstration of God's unbreakable purpose. The curse was never possible; the blessing was always sure.

Balaam's own end, we learn later in Scripture, was tragic. He spoke magnificent truths about God yet never truly gave his heart to Him, and he came to a sorrowful end (Num 31:8). His story is a solemn warning: it is possible to be near the things of God, to speak of Him wonderfully, and still be lost.

The question "Who can live when God does this?" finds its answer only in Christ. When God's judgment falls, the one hope of survival is to be hidden in the Saviour. He is the refuge from the storm, the One in whom we can stand when all else is shaken (Rom 8:1). Do not merely speak of God like Balaam; give Him your heart and find life in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is it possible to know about God without truly knowing Him?
2. What does Balaam's tragic end warn you about?
3. Where do you find your safety when God's judgment is in view?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from being like Balaam, who spoke of You yet never gave You his heart. Draw me to know You truly and to find my refuge in Christ alone. Amen.
